text: Are there any E. coli expression studies about ciprofloxacin?

## Abstract

This study investigates the availability of expression profiling studies in Escherichia coli related to ciprofloxacin, using the NCBI GEO database. The query retrieved 37 total GEO Series (GSE) records matching "Escherichia coli" and "ciprofloxacin," with metadata for the top 10 studies shown. These studies cover a range of topics including stress responses, antibiotic resistance, and transcriptomic changes upon ciprofloxacin exposure. Results provide researchers with evidence that relevant omics datasets exist for E. coli under ciprofloxacin treatment, supporting further analysis of antibiotic response and resistance mechanisms.

## I. Introduction

### Background

Ciprofloxacin is a widely used fluoroquinolone antibiotic, and Escherichia coli is a common Gram-negative bacterium, frequent target of antimicrobial research. Understanding the transcriptomic response of E. coli to ciprofloxacin can reveal mechanisms of drug tolerance, resistance, and stress adaptation.

### Literature Review

No PubMed records were formally linked to the query via GEO for all studies, but some have associated PMIDs. For example, GSE276254 is linked to PMID 40879398, and GSE295494 is linked to PMID 41805196.

### Knowledge Gap

Prior to this query, the number and nature of expression studies in E. coli involving ciprofloxacin were undefined.

### Objective & Hypothesis

Objective: To identify whether expression studies in E. coli exist that involve ciprofloxacin. Hypothesis: GEO contains multiple such datasets, reflecting a diversity of experimental contexts.

## II. Materials and Methods

### Study Design

A search for gene expression studies (GEO Series) was performed with the organism "Escherichia coli" and keyword "ciprofloxacin".

### Materials

- NCBI GEO, accessed via functions.geo_search

### Procedures

- Tool called with: organism="Escherichia coli", term="ciprofloxacin", entry_type="gse", max_results=10
- Return includes Series accession, title, summary, sample, platform, date, and file links.

### Statistical Analysis

- The returned result summarized the total count (`total_count`) among the database, and metadata for the first 10 records. The denominator is the GEO Series database filtered for organism and keyword.

## III. Results

### Data Presentation

#### Table 1: Selected E. coli GEO Series Studies Involving Ciprofloxacin

| Accession   | Title                                                                      | Sample Count | Date Public  | Platform   | FTP Directory                                      |
|-------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------|--------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| GSE309890   | Antidepressant sertraline & resistance emergence (pentose phosphate pathway) | 6            | 2026-02-01   | GPL24659   | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/ |
| GSE276254   | Antimicrobial peptide BTP-001 and resistance to ciprofloxacin              | 51           | 2025-08-25   | GPL21222   | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE276nnn/GSE276254/ |
| GSE283264   | 3D genome organization in E. coli (RNA-Seq)                               | 25           | 2025-06-24   | GPL32081   | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE283nnn/GSE283264/ |
| GSE295494   | Early transcriptomic responses in E. coli to antibiotic exposure           | 42           | 2025-05-01   | GPL26592   | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE295nnn/GSE295494/ |
| GSE292923   | Effect of purA on transcriptome during ciprofloxacin treatment             | 4            | 2025-03-25   | GPL18133   | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE292nnn/GSE292923/ |
| GSE275261   | IMPDH/GuaB inhibition in A. baumannii and E. coli (ciprofloxacin control)  | 24           | 2024-08-25   | GPL22143   | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE275nnn/GSE275261/ |

#### Summary: 37 studies found, metadata for top 10 shown.

### Findings

There are 37 expression profiling GEO Series records for Escherichia coli involving ciprofloxacin. The presented data include varied experimental designs, including antibiotic adaptation, resistance, and genetic manipulation.

## IV. Discussion

### Interpretation

These results confirm that expression datasets for E. coli under ciprofloxacin exposure are available, supporting analysis of drug response at the transcriptome level.

### Context

Linked PubMed IDs and study summaries indicate that several records focus on resistance mechanisms, stress responses, and metabolic shifts as part of the E. coli response to ciprofloxacin.

### Limitations

- Only metadata is available via API; expression values (counts, matrices) require downloading from FTP links.
- Only the top 10 records are shown due to truncation; full list includes 37.
- PubMed linkage is incomplete in GEO.

### Conclusion & Future Directions

E. coli expression studies about ciprofloxacin are well-represented in GEO. Future work could download underlying matrices for in-depth analysis or focus on newer studies with multi-omics design.

[7] NCBI GEO API: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi
